newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rikadenki fails to honour 2nd promissory note.
newsitem.headline: Rikadenki fails to honour 2nd promissory note.

text.p: Japan's Rikadenki Kogyo Co Ltd said on Friday that banks are likely to suspend its right to make fresh transactions as of March 5, as it had failed to honour promissory notes for a second time.
Rikadenki said in a statement that it had not decided whether to continue its business or restructure, but added that it would make public its decision soon.

The company is traded on the over-the-counter market, and Rikadenki said it would ask market authorities to put its shares under surveillance. The shares were ask-only at 205 yen on Friday, compared with Thursday's level of 365 yen.
The announcement came two days after the company confirmed that it had a problem in honouring promissory notes.

The company's shares were suspended from trade on Wednesday afternoon after private research company Teikoku Databank said in a report that the company had failed to honour promissory notes for the first time last Friday.

Rikadenki, which makes various measurement instruments, said it had suffered from falling prices for its mainstay industrial measuring products in the face of tough competition from domestic rivals. It has posted a current loss for eight successive years, it said.
